claims.text: In situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction is effective for characterizing high-temperature oxidation behaviour.
In situ high-temperature X-ray diffraction is effective for characterizing phase stability.
HT-XRD enables real-time monitoring of phase transformations during heating.
HT-XRD enables real-time monitoring of oxide formation during heating in an oxidizing environment.
The proposed initial material has a well-characterized room-temperature phase composition and negligible oxide content.
The material is heated in an oxygen-containing atmosphere using a high-temperature stage integrated with an XRD instrument.
Diffraction-peak evolution can indicate formation of new oxide phases.
Diffraction-peak evolution can indicate alterations in the original phase structure.
Thermal activation in an oxidizing atmosphere causes oxidation of the material.
Heating can cause phase transformations in the material.
Oxidation and phase transformations are detected through shifts, emergence, or disappearance of diffraction peaks.
Heating in an oxidizing atmosphere is predicted to produce new diffraction peaks corresponding to oxide phases.
Heating is predicted to produce shifts, intensity changes, or disappearance of peaks from the original phases.
HT-XRD may have limited sensitivity to trace oxide formation or early-stage phase changes.
Complementary techniques may be required to verify trace oxidation or early-stage phase changes.
